text:
anya: kicking off a small canary to probe a phased microwindow policy (reduce microbatch interval -> 2ms, coalesce delay -> 6ms, jitter +-1.5ms). seeing unexpected KV hit churn and tail rise, posting initial traces + plan

sam: can you drop the perf numbers you saw? p99/p95/p50?

anya: baseline (stable pool) p50=12ms p95=92ms p99=260ms. canary after change p50=14ms p95=138ms p99=480ms. token throughput roughly same but CPU on host is spiking. KV hit rate down ~12%.

mike: hm KV hit drop suggests priming or eviction pattern changed. did coalesce change affect KV token alignment?

anya: probable — when we shorten micro-interval we break longer prefix groups and cause more unique cache keys. also saw kernel selection flip to fused_attn_v2 on some shards (profiler trace attached).

lee: did the runtime fall back to different kernel because seq-len distribution changed? fused_attn_v2 has worse cold-cache memory use for kv pages on 80-token windows.

anya: yes, kernel selector metrics show increased fused_attn_v2 load on 2 GPUs of canary. profiler snippet: ```kernel_selector: chosen=fused_attn_v2 reasons=[latency_hint, small_batch_estimate]```

sam: maybe the selector heuristic mis-estimated cost due to microbatching changing effective batch shapes. we should log batch shape histograms per decision point.

mike: agree. also suspect our token budget gating allowed slightly larger microbatches when jitter aligned; that can push internal kernel tiling to unfavorable dims.

anya: attached small flamegraph and KV miss timeline. Misses correlate with short-lived cache churn windows right after config flip.

infra-bot: deploy canary update completed: canary-pool v2.3.7 -> microwindow-config applied to 6 hosts.

lee: quick experiment proposal: enable adaptive jitter (targeted to reduce alignment with token boundaries): jitter = base * (1 + random_gauss(0, 0.6)), and temporarily bias kernel_selector to prefer aten_fp16 when kv_hit_rate < 0.8. Run 30m, collect histograms.

sam: +1. add metric: "batch_shape_entropy" and emit to console. also add KV priming warmup for first 200ms after coalesce delay change to avoid eviction storms.

mike: caution on priming — it increases short-term token cost. but for canary it's fine. can we test a config diff? Suggested patch snippet: ```
microbatch_interval_ms: 2
coalesce_delay_ms: 6
jitter_ms: { distribution: adaptive, sigma: 0.6 }
kernel_bias: { prefer: ["aten_fp16"], condition: "kv_hit_rate < 0.8" }
kv_priming_window_ms: 200
```

anya: creating a Jira to track. will run 3 variations: (A) adaptive jitter + kernel bias, (B) longer coalesce 8ms + small jitter, (C) baseline microinterval but with priming. will snapshot p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, batch_shape_entropy, kernel_mix.

jira-bot: Created RED-9482: "microwindow phased probe: adaptive jitter, kernel bias, KV priming canary" assigned to anya.

lee: FYI if we bias kernel selection we need to ensure we keep a fallback policy if memory or perf degrades — automatic unbias after 5% SLA breach.

anya: noted. I'll add an SLA watchdog that reverts the bias if p99 > baseline*1.4 for >2m.

sam: one more thought — token budget targets: maybe our per-request token budget rounding interacts with microbatch slotting. If budget target is rounded up in aggregated step it can push a request into next kernel tile. add metric: "token_budget_roundups".

mike: agree. also capture per-batch kernel tile dims and the chosen kernel id to correlate with tail spikes.

anya: running A/B/C now, 10-min warmup then 30m collection. will post TL;DR and raw traces here. @lee @sam please watch alerts. :thumbsup:

lee: ack :eyes:

infra-bot: canary-alert: host g9-03 high mem growth during test A at 1987654371 (OOM avoided).

anya: saw that — OOM near priming window on host g9-03. taking host out of canary and decreasing priming window to 120ms for A. continuing.

sam: provisional observation after 15m: A reduced p99 on 4/6 hosts (median down 18%) but 2 hosts had memory churn. B seems stable but less improvement (~6% p99). C shows no meaningful change.

mike: that's promising. can we get kernel_mix: A -> aten_fp16 62%, fused_attn_v2 35%, other 3%. Baseline was aten_fp16 45% fused 52%.

anya: KV hit rate rebound in A to baseline+3% on healthy hosts, but the two bad hosts still had periodic thrash. hypothesis: priming loads pushed ephemeral pages into memory causing GC pressure on certain CUDA drivers.

lee: we should exclude hosts with older driver or smaller reserved kernel heap from the canary until we understand. log their driver version and CUDA mem alloc patterns.

anya: pulling logs and consolidating into RED-9482. next steps: narrow priming to 100ms, keep adaptive jitter, implement token_budget_roundups metric, add kernel selector telemetry. will re-run canary after driver check.

sam: also add a lightweight offline sim that replays arrival traces with new microwindows to predict kernel mix shifts before deploying. saves time.

anya: agreed — I'll queue the sim job and will post results. thanks all. :rocket:
